extra.reason: README.md and extension-icon.png created and committed on chore/add-readme-and-icon
Replaced iStats with downloaded iSMC binary. Verified against real Apple Silicon output: fan=F<n>Ac actual speed (2632rpm), CPU temp tiered (CPU Die Max 79.1C). Build clean.
Resized assets/extension-icon.png 644x644 → 512x512 via sips; ray lint 'validate extension icons' now passes (ready).

Root cause was NOT eslint 10 — eslint 9.39.4 crashed identically. @raycast/eslint-config exports a top-level array with a nested config array at index 5; [...spread] only flattened one level, leaving the inner array to trip @eslint/config-array's normalizer ('Unexpected array'). Fix: eslint.config.js now uses raycastConfig.flat(Infinity). Also pinned eslint ^10→^9 to stay within typescript-eslint@8's supported peer range (^8.57||^9, not 10), matching the config's bundled v9 deps. ray lint 'run ESLint' now ready.

Handle 'kumamaki' now registered on Raycast (api/v1/users/kumamaki -> 200). package.json author was already 'kumamaki', so no code change needed — ray lint 'validate package.json file' now ready. All four ray lint checks pass.

Rewrote Prerequisites; removed dead 'gem install iStats' (gone since d8390ef). Added 'Sensor data and iSMC' section disclosing the first-run download + exec of the third-party GPL-3.0 iSMC binary (v0.16.5, SHA256-verified, cached) and graceful degradation. Fixed npm->pnpm in install/dev. stop-slop pass on prose. ray lint Prettier passes.

Normalize ps pcpu by os.cpus().length in getTopProcesses so ProcessStat.cpu is a 0-100% share of total machine capacity. ps reports cores×100% summed; gauges (cpuColor 70/40/15, deriveThermalPressure 90/50 fallback, diagnosisText >=30) were calibrated for 0-100 and are now correct without rescaling. formatStatsForAI rounds to 1dp and labels the scale as % of total machine. Chose normalize over relabel-across-cores for the consumer 'how hot is my machine' framing. ray build + lint green.

diagnosisText now gates 'overloading your CPU' on top.cpu>=70 (normalized machine share). When thermal pressure is heavy/critical but no process is maxing the CPU, it reports 'Running hot (95°C), but no process is maxing the CPU' instead of falsely blaming the top process. Fixes the observed '(3%) is overloading' nonsense. ray build + lint green.

Rebuilt heat model. system.ts now exposes collectSnapshot() -> SystemSnapshot (measured: cpuTempC, fanRpm, fanMaxRpm, loadPct, coreCount, powerSource, isCharging, memoryPressure, topProcesses, sensorsAvailable) and buildVerdict() -> {level: cool|busy|hot, cause: cpu|busy|charging|ambient|none, headline, detail}. New live signals: os.loadavg() total load, iSMC F<n>Mx fan-%-of-max, pmset -g ps charging/power. Throttle (pmset -g therm) verified DEAD on Apple Silicon under full load -> deferred to heatcheck-6bi (Swift thermalState helper). Headline generated from cause so a 3% process can never read as 'overloading'. heat-check.tsx redesigned verdict-first with Temperature/Fan(%max)/CPU Load/Power/Memory rows; dropped the temp-derived Thermal Pressure row. diagnosis.tsx + AI/display formatters updated; AI prompt now told Apple Silicon runs 90-100C by design. Parsers verified against live output. ray build + lint green. Supersedes heatcheck-6qg (diagnosisText fix folded in).
Added 'warm' thermal band (yellow). buildVerdict now computes a 3-state thermal axis (none/warm/hot) at 70%/85% fan and 85/95C, with heat outranking compute. Verified building + against live sensors.

SystemSnapshot now carries TempReadings (cpu max+avg, gpu, ssd, battery) and FanReading[] (per-fan rpm/max). Shown in heat-check List (Temperatures + per-fan rows), diagnosis Detail, and AI context. Parsers verified against live iSMC JSON.
